question: What are the five main OT covenants typically identified in Catholic and evangelical biblical theology?

choices.A: Noahic, Abrahamic, Mosaic, Davidic, and New (Jeremiah 31)
choices.B: Edenic, Adamic, Abrahamic, Mosaic, and Noahic
choices.C: Abrahamic, Mosaic, Solomonic, Prophetic, and Messianic
choices.D: Creation, Flood, Sinai, Temple, and Exile

teaching.title: The Five Major Covenants
teaching.body: The five covenants form the backbone of OT salvation history: (1) Noahic (Gen 9) — universal, with all humanity and creation; no more flood; sign = rainbow. (2) Abrahamic (Gen 12-17) — land, descendants, blessing to all nations; sign = circumcision. (3) Mosaic (Exod 19-24) — Sinai covenant with Israel; Torah stipulations; sign = Sabbath. (4) Davidic (2 Sam 7) — eternal dynasty and kingdom; God's 'son' on the throne. (5) New Covenant (Jer 31:31-34) — internalized law, universal forgiveness; fulfilled in Christ (Luke 22:20, Heb 8-9). Each covenant builds on and expands the previous.
